# Expected round-by-round results for
# testdata/scottish/highland-2022-badenoch-and-strathspey.blt, transcribed from Highland
# Council's official "Candidate Votes Per Stage Report" for the 2022 Badenoch and Strathspey
# ward count (8 candidates, 4 seats, 5529 valid votes, quota 1106). Values are exact fractions
# in the same lowest-terms form info.fkhodkov.rankedchoice.core.util.Fraction prints them in,
# so comparison against the engine's actual output is exact equality, not decimal rounding.
#
# Every tally value below has been independently spot-checked against the official report's
# published 5-decimal-place figures (e.g. round 2's "11251709/12500" == the official
# "900.13672" for Cockburn) and matches exactly.
#
# Note on round 8: the official report shows Bruce's final-seat election with a "true" surplus
# of 111.62324 (1217.62324 - 1106 quota). Our engine instead reports a surplus of Fraction.ZERO
# for this round, because by round 8 Bruce is the only continuing candidate and exactly one
# seat remains — the engine's documented "remaining continuing == remaining seats" shortcut
# elects him outright rather than computing a real surplus. This is a deliberate, documented
# engine convention (see RoundAction.Elected's javadoc), not a discrepancy in the underlying
# tally, so round 8's action line below omits an expected surplus rather than asserting 0 or
# 111.62324 — the test must treat a missing surplus as "not checked" for this round.
#
# Note on "exhausted": each round's WIGM transfer truncates its per-parcel ratio to 5 decimal
# places (per the "scottish" ruleset), which loses a tiny fraction of the surplus to rounding
# on every transfer (e.g. round 1: surplus 174 / 1280 ballots truncates to 0.13593, one step
# short of the exact 0.1359375, losing 0.00960 votes). The official report tracks this as a
# separate "non-transferable votes (due to rounding)" line so its grand total always reconciles
# to exactly 5529.00000; our engine has no such separate bucket — the lost fraction simply
# isn't attributed anywhere; it doesn't appear in any candidate's tally, and it doesn't appear
# in "exhausted" either. As a result, the "exhausted" values below match the official report's
# "Non-transferable votes" line exactly (both track only real, ballot-exhaustion-caused
# non-transferability), but do NOT include that separate rounding-loss line, and the sum of a
# round's tallies + exhausted will therefore be a little short of 5529 by the rounding loss
# accumulated so far. This is expected and does not affect who gets elected.
